findings.title: Resumable-upload bridge attaches a new EvidencePart to any same-team evidence — including SIGNED/REPORTED or another member's in-flight record — and the next report run then declares sealed evidence FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH

plans: all with a shared workspace or integrations

evidence.snippet: const owningEvidence = await client.evidence.findFirst({ where: { id: input.evidenceId, teamId: input.teamId }, select: { id: true } });
const partRow = await client.evidencePart.create({ data: { evidenceId: session.evidence_id, partIndex: session.target_part_index, ... sha256: serverSha256 } })
legacy parts route: owner-only (403) and SIGNED/REPORTED/lockedAt -> 409, advisory lock, validateUploadedFile
prisma.evidencePart.findMany({ where: { evidenceId: evidence.id }, orderBy: { partIndex: "asc" } ... }) — no artifactClass/uploadedAtUtc filter
fileSha256 = hashes.length === 1 ? hashes[0] : sha256HexFromStrings(hashes); if (fileSha256 !== evidence.fileSha256 ...) await rejectEvidenceIntegrity({...})
transition to FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH + custody rejection event

findings.observed: Session creation proves only that the evidence id exists in the caller's team. The multipart-complete bridge never re-reads the evidence and inserts an EvidencePart (uploadedAtUtc NULL) at the session's targetPartIndex. No DB trigger forbids parts on sealed evidence; the (evidenceId, partIndex) unique key is dodged by an unused index. The report worker enumerates ALL parts unfiltered and recomputes the composite; the extra part makes it differ from evidence.fileSha256 and rejectEvidenceIntegrity moves the record to FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH with a custody rejection event.
findings.expected: Parts may be added only by the evidence owner (or intake uploader) while the record is CREATED/UPLOADING, not locked, not held, not deleted — the same guards the legacy /v1/evidence/:id/parts route applies — re-checked inside the bridge transaction.
findings.dataFlow: POST /v1/uploads/sessions {teamId,evidenceId:E(SIGNED),targetPartIndex:9999} -> initiate -> presign -> PUT -> multipart/complete {verifyHash:true} -> evidence_parts INSERT -> (report/recovery/updated-report run) -> processor multipart rehash mismatch -> evidences.status=FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH + custody INTEGRITY rejection
findings.rootCause: The Phase 30.12 bridge was added as a second EvidencePart writer without the legacy route's state/owner/lock guards; the worker treats every EvidencePart as original material.
findings.blastRadius: Every evidence record in any workspace where a second member holds evidence.create, plus any workspace with an integration key holding integration.evidence.upload. Scenario B: injection into another member's UPLOADING record gets the attacker's bytes signed into the victim's custody with uploadedByUserId NULL.
findings.impact: A sealed evidence record can be made to read as tampered (FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH is terminal and suppresses verify/report), and foreign bytes can be sealed into another custodian's record — custody/integrity corruption.
findings.reproduction: As CONTRIBUTOR in team T with SIGNED evidence E owned by another member: create an upload session targeting E with an unused targetPartIndex, complete the multipart upload with verifyHash:true, then trigger any report run for E (updated report / lifecycle recovery).
findings.runtimeProofIdea: Integration probe on disposable PG: seed team + SIGNED evidence owned by user A, call createUploadSession as CONTRIBUTOR B -> expect evidence_not_found/refusal; observe it succeeds. Then call the bridge path (completeStorageMultipart with a local storage stub for S3 head/complete) and count evidence_parts before/after.
findings.remediation: Route every EvidencePart write through one guarded writer: require owner (or intake principal), status IN (CREATED, UPLOADING), lockedAt NULL, deletedAt NULL, no active legal hold — asserted in the same transaction as the insert with a row lock; refuse session creation on the same predicate; make the worker ignore parts whose uploadedAtUtc is NULL.
findings.acceptanceProof: Integration test: session creation and bridge both refuse for SIGNED/REPORTED/locked/held/other-owner evidence; a report run over a record with a stray NULL-uploadedAt part does not reject integrity.
findings.migrationBackfill: Scan production for evidence_parts with uploaded_at_utc NULL on evidences whose status is SIGNED/REPORTED, and for FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH rows whose extra part came from a bridged session.

findings.title: One aborted or expired upload session blocks finalization of its evidence forever; the idempotency key returns the terminal session on retry

evidence.snippet: evaluateUploadSessionFinalizeGate denies for ANY session not COMPLETED
WHERE "team_id" = $1 AND "idempotency_key" = $2 LIMIT 1 — no state filter despite 'non-terminal' comment

findings.observed: Any non-COMPLETED session on an evidence id denies finalization; nothing deletes/supersedes sessions; the retry reuses the same key and gets the ABORTED/EXPIRED session back, whose initiate fails session_already_terminal. Any team member with evidence.create can create or abort a session on another member's evidence.
findings.expected: A terminal session must not block finalization, and a retry must mint a fresh session; session mutation limited to the session actor/evidence owner.
findings.dataFlow: cancel/expire session -> completeEvidence -> evaluateUploadSessionFinalizeGate -> 409 session_aborted/session_expired forever; evidence stays UPLOADING (no Evidence reaper)
findings.rootCause: Finalize gate treats ABORTED/EXPIRED the same as in-flight; idempotency lookup ignores state.
findings.blastRadius: Every resumable (large-file) web capture that is cancelled or left idle ~1h.
findings.impact: Evidence permanently stuck UPLOADING and (per ACQ-02) counted against the FREE record cap; teammate griefing possible.
findings.reproduction: Start a resumable capture, abort it (or let reapStaleUploadSessions expire it), retry: complete returns 409 indefinitely.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: Integration: create session, abort, call evaluateUploadSessionFinalizeGate -> denial; recreate with same key -> reused terminal row.
findings.remediation: Ignore terminal sessions in the finalize gate (or require only that no ACTIVE session exists), filter the idempotency lookup to non-terminal rows, and restrict session mutations to the session actor/evidence owner.
findings.acceptanceProof: Test: abort then retry completes; teammate cannot abort another member's session.
findings.migrationBackfill: Identify evidences stuck UPLOADING with only terminal sessions.

findings.title: Idempotent session reuse does not check the returned session belongs to the requested evidenceId

evidence.snippet: lookup keyed on (team_id, idempotency_key) only; returns existing[0] regardless of evidence_id

findings.observed: A same-team member who pre-creates key capture:<X>:<i> bound to their own evidence Y diverts the victim's upload for X to Y's storage key and bridge.
findings.expected: Reuse only when evidence_id (and actor) match; otherwise 409.
findings.dataFlow: POST sessions {evidenceId:X, idempotencyKey:k} -> returns session for Y
findings.rootCause: Idempotency key not bound to its request parameters.
findings.blastRadius: Narrow: attacker needs X's id before the victim's large-item loop.
findings.impact: Victim's bytes land on another record.
findings.reproduction: Create session with key capture:X:0 for evidence Y; victim's client reuses it.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: unit on createUploadSession with fake client
findings.remediation: Compare evidence_id/actor on reuse; refuse mismatch.

findings.title: seed-home-personas.ts writes fabricated SIGNED evidence and custody into whatever DATABASE_URL dotenv loads, guarded only by NODE_ENV

evidence.snippet: sibling script has a DB-name guard this one lacks

findings.observed: The script loads services/api/.env (which, per standing project knowledge, carries live production credentials) and has no database-name guard, so running it without NODE_ENV=production writes fabricated trust rows to whatever DB that file names.
findings.expected: Same DB-name/loopback guard as seed-admin-fixture.ts and no implicit dotenv load.
findings.dataFlow: pnpm seed:home-personas -> dotenv -> DATABASE_URL -> raw prisma.evidence.create + custodyEvent.createMany
findings.rootCause: Guard copied inconsistently across seed scripts.
findings.blastRadius: Operator workstation only; not remotely reachable.
findings.impact: Fabricated custody records in a real database if misrun.
findings.reproduction: Not executed (would contact the configured DB).
findings.remediation: Add the seed-admin-fixture DB-name/loopback guard and drop dotenv/config.

findings.title: Multipart path never enforces expectedTotalBytes/partSizeBytes, marks parts VERIFIED without a reference hash, and leaves bridged parts without uploadedByUserId

evidence.snippet: parts marked VERIFIED when expected_sha256 is NULL

findings.observed: expectedTotalBytes never compared to head.contentLength; VERIFIED set with no reference; attribution missing on bridged parts. Server whole-object hash still reflects real bytes, so this is not tampering.
findings.expected: Enforce declared size, do not label VERIFIED without a reference, record uploader.
findings.rootCause: Hygiene gaps in the Phase 30.12 path.
findings.impact: Misleading VERIFIED label; lost uploader attribution in custody.
findings.remediation: Enforce sizes; use UNVERIFIED_NO_REFERENCE; set uploadedByUserId from the session actor.
